tourism.route: Visitor visa/visa exemption as currently published
tourism.detail: Australian visitors should use the current DHA entry and stay instructions; the exact admission period is set under the immigration rules and border decision.

meetings.detail: Meetings and conference/business attendance can fit a visitor purpose when no South African employment or remuneration is undertaken.
meetings.next: Keep negotiation separate from local delivery and employment.
meetings.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

conference.detail: A delegate or visitor is different from paid programme delivery, training or performance.
conference.next: Ask the organiser whether a prescribed-activity or work route is needed.
conference.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

unpaid-speaking.detail: Unpaid speaking can still be work-like. South African immigration categories turn on the activity, host and duration rather than the fee alone.
unpaid-speaking.next: Have the host check DHA's prescribed-activity visitor/work requirements.
unpaid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

paid-speaking.route: General work, critical-skills or prescribed-activity visa
paid-speaking.detail: Paid speaking, consulting, teaching and employment need a South African work authorisation or an applicable prescribed-activity exemption/category.
paid-speaking.next: Ask the engager to identify the exact DHA visa and supporting employer documents.
paid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

book-launch.route: Visitor for rights; work/cultural route for paid launch
book-launch.detail: Publisher meetings may be business travel; paid launch delivery, workshops, local retail and performance need the activity route.
book-launch.next: Separate author fee, royalties, expenses and sales.
book-launch.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

ai-teaching.detail: University exchange and paid professional training need different host evidence and possibly work permission.
ai-teaching.next: Have the university/company state the appointment, payment and duration.
ai-teaching.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

remote-work.detail: DHA publishes requirements for a remote-work visitor visa and states that its holder is not entitled to take employment in South Africa.
remote-work.next: Check income, tax-registration and stay conditions and keep South African clients/employment outside the route.
remote-work.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

entrepreneur.detail: Founder operation and investment are not covered by ordinary visitor entry; business and critical-skills categories require a prepared case.
entrepreneur.next: Choose investor, business, critical-skills or employer route with DHA/DTIC guidance.
entrepreneur.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

trade.route: Visitor business route; local fulfilment needs work/customs status
trade.detail: Meetings, sourcing and trade fairs can be visitor activity; installation, sales and service delivery may require permission.
trade.next: Map South African importer, customer and on-site work.
trade.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

artist.detail: Paid performance, filming, exhibition and music work should be checked with the promoter and DHA.
artist.next: Have the producer state venue, contract, fee, crew and dates.
artist.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

mixed-mission.route: Visitor front door plus DHA activation
mixed-mission.detail: South Africa can support English-first conferences and a remote base, but local delivery remains a separate immigration key.
mixed-mission.next: Break the itinerary into visitor, remote, paid local and cultural activity.
mixed-mission.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

filming.route: Visitor's visa with work authorisation (STAGES scheme for accredited partners)
filming.detail: Foreign crews working for a foreign employer use a visitor's visa with work authorisation. The STAGES scheme simplifies this for accredited film-industry partners.
filming.next: Use an accredited local service company.

laws.rule: SARS lists a duty-free allowance of 2 litres of wine and 1 litre of other alcohol per person. It does not apply to anyone under 18.

laws.rule: SARS lists a duty-free allowance of 200 cigarettes and 20 cigars, plus 250 g of cigarette or pipe tobacco, per person. It does not apply to anyone under 18. The page does not address e-cigarettes.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: Commercial, corporate and non-profit RPAS work needs an Unmanned Aircraft Systems Operating Certificate (UASOC), an RPAS Letter of Approval, a Remote Pilot Licence and registration. Foreigners need a passport to sit RPAS exams; SACAA evaluates foreign licences. No visitor route confirmed.

items.text: Not yet checked: no public SACAA directory of UASOC holders was found on the pages read.

Under Part 101 an RPAS may be operated only with a UASOC. The aircraft needs an RPAS Letter of Approval and registration. A Remote Pilot Licence follows training at a SACAA-approved training organisation. The table on SACAA's page marks the letter, licence and registration as required for commercial, corporate and non-profit operations, and not applicable for private ones.

SACAA's FAQ says foreigners need a passport to sit RPAS exams, and SACAA says it evaluates foreign licences and may consult the issuing state. How a visiting foreign operator gets approval was not read.

South African Tourism's Digital Assets library has login and register links, and per a search summary holds images and video clips for promoting travel to South Africa; registered users get access by permission and must accept its terms. Aerial footage and the full licence text were not confirmed (the 2025 user manual was too large to open).
